interpretation: one or two gold-specific terms suffice; a rewriter that sees only the question has a plausible chance -- run the reformulation producer before funding cards
scope_limits: ORACLE: the added terms come from the gold text itself. A real rewriter sees only the question, so every distance here is a LOWER bound on what a real producer must achieve.
Rarity is estimated over the 153,602-document Sidecar X sample, not the whole 947k corpus; terms absent from the sample are treated as rarest, which favours the oracle.
Reach into the BM25 top-50 is admission, not delivery: gold still has to survive fusion and the seat cut.
ERB pool-absent cohort on one bed; the semantic class is generated under an explicit anti-lexical instruction.

contamination.what: The oracle's candidate terms were ranked by rarity with no guessability filter, so the rarest term in a gold chunk is almost always the document's own 32-hex UUID (e.g. 22a7e9af2760474dbdf611c2c21cd231, 730ed8ee5fc84e0b9be761003b9a60d3). Adding a document's identifier retrieves that document trivially.
contamination.why_it_invalidates: No query rewriter can produce a UUID it has never seen, so the measured distances say nothing about whether reformulation is a viable producer. The headline 109/109 reachable at median distance 2 is an artefact of identifier tokens.
contamination.fix: candidate terms must be alphabetic AND appear in >= 5 sample documents (--min-df 5, alphabetic-only), so the oracle may use real domain vocabulary and never an identifier
